purpose: Determine whether public primary sources provide a complete clean-room prescription for the historical SEOBNRv4 conservative Hamiltonian through the calibrated radial-potential block. This is a source-completeness gate, not a numerical proximity gate.

bohe_2017.citation: Bohé et al., Phys. Rev. D 95, 044028 (2017), arXiv:1611.03703v3, Sec. II.A, Eqs. (2.1)-(2.3) (PDF p. 3; source paper.tex lines 250-297), and Sec. IV.C, Eqs. (4.12)-(4.14) (PDF pp. 9-10; source paper.tex lines 751-778)

barausse_buonanno_2011.citation: Barausse and Buonanno, Phys. Rev. D 84, 104027 (2011), arXiv:1107.2904v2, Eqs. (50)-(54) (PDF p. 8; source paper.tex lines 824-902)

steinhoff_2016.citation: Steinhoff et al., Phys. Rev. D 94, 104028 (2016), arXiv:1608.01907v2, Appendix A, Eqs. (A1)-(A2h) (PDF pp. 23-24; source dyntide_ham.tex lines 2045-2085)

mandatory_requirements.description: A public primary source specifies the real/effective EOB energy map and normalization.
A public primary source specifies the effective spinning Hamiltonian structure and the dynamical spin map used by the model lineage.
Public primary sources specify the radial-potential value, Delta_0 through Delta_5 coefficients, and the SEOBNRv4 4PN correction.
A public primary source prints the SEOBNRv4 K, d_SO, and d_SS calibration fits.
A public primary source identifies the exact coefficient precision and rounding retained by the historical implementation.
A public primary source explicitly specifies the historical radial derivative of the logarithmic potential, including every logarithmic contribution and any implementation-specific omission.

pass_rule: Every mandatory requirement must be satisfied by the pinned public primary sources. Analytic completion of an unstated historical derivative convention, GPL implementation source, binary-oracle output, or numerical retuning cannot fill a missing field.
clean_room_exclusions: Do not inspect or transcribe LALSimulation source to fill a missing prescription field.
Do not query or fit to a LALSimulation binary oracle.
Do not infer retained decimals or a derivative convention from numerical proximity.
Do not retune a coefficient, formula, or threshold.
